acceptanceCriteria: A machine-readable impact capability listing names suffixes with rules, suffixes admitted without rules, and per-call limits; or impact reports unadmitted paths as unanalysed instead of refusing the call.
The listing is derived from the same table the admission code uses, with a test that they agree.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1304 (opened 2026-10-20). Feature request; not yet specified. **Observed.** Which paths `corvint impact` accepts depends on the immutable index: some suffixes get reverse-import rules (Go/Ruby/JS/TS), other indexed suffixes (for example `.json`) are accepted with a missing-rule uncertainty, and unindexed suffixes return `unsupported-impact-path-suffix` for the whole call. The only description is prose in `--help`, so a consumer must hard-code its own suffix list to avoid a whole-call refusal. **Wanted.** A machine-readable capability listing (for example `corvint impact --capabilities --json`) naming suffixes with rules, suffixes admitted without rules, and the per-call limits (path count, `--limit` range); or an option to report unadmitted paths in the receipt as `unanalysed` instead of refusing the call. See beamfall/corvint#1304 for the full text.
title: No machine-readable list of admitted impact path suffixes (issue #1304)
